speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You presented with gait and limb ataxia along with a significant medical history; to begin our assessment, how long have you been experiencing these balance and coordination issues?

speaker: Patient
text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds concerning; since the clumsiness is more prominent on your right side, is this a new problem, or have you had similar episodes in the past? REQUEST TEST: MRI_Brain to check for structural lesions or atrophy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: MRI_Brain Findings: Lesions consistent with Progressive Multifocal Encephalopathy (PML). Comments: T1/T2 images showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without gadolinium enhancement, indicative of PML.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML).

The MRI results showing multifocal demyelinating lesions without enhancement are classic for PML, an opportunistic infection of the white matter usually caused by the JC virus, which is often seen in patients with compromised immune systems like HIV/AIDS. Were you diagnosed with HIV or taking immunosuppressive medications such as natalizumab or rituximab?
